1: """Track 03 - Dexterous hands.
2: 
3: Hands differ from arms in three ways that these exercises cover: many joints
4: are mechanically coupled, the task is defined by several fingertips at once,
5: and the joint ranges are small enough that limits are hit all the time.
6: """
7: 
8: import numpy as np
9: 
10: 
11: def is_force_closure(contacts, normals, mu):
12:     """Does a planar two-finger grasp resist an arbitrary wrench?
13: 
14:     Two point contacts with friction hold an object if, and only if, the
15:     line joining them lies inside both friction cones. Then the fingers can
16:     squeeze along that line, and the friction available at each end covers
17:     every direction the object could otherwise slip.
18: 
19:     With ``d`` the unit vector from contact 0 to contact 1, the grasp needs
20:     the force at contact 0 to point along ``+d`` and the one at contact 1
21:     along ``-d``, each within its own cone of half-angle ``arctan(mu)``.
22: 
23:     Compare the components rather than the angles. Splitting a direction
24:     ``u`` against a unit normal ``n`` the same way ``friction_cone`` does::
25: 
26:         along  = dot(u, n)
27:         across = norm(u - along * n)
28: 
29:     the direction is inside the cone when ``along > 0`` and
30:     ``across <= mu * along``. That is the same test as
31:     ``angle(u, n) <= arctan(mu)``, but ``arccos`` near 1 turns a rounding
32:     error of 1e-16 into 1e-8 and reports a perfectly good diagonal grasp as
33:     slipping.
34: 
35:     Checking only that the normals oppose each other is not enough. Every
36:     antipodal pair passes that test, and a pair whose normals are tilted
37:     away from the line slips as soon as ``mu`` is small.
38: 
39:     * ``contacts``: ``(2, 2)``, the two contact points in the plane.
40:     * ``normals``: ``(2, 2)``, the inward surface normal at each contact,
41:       not necessarily unit length.
42:     * ``mu >= 0``, the friction coefficient.
43:

2: 
3: Hands differ from arms in three ways that these exercises cover: many joints
4: are mechanically coupled, the task is defined by several fingertips at once,
5: and the joint ranges are small enough that limits are hit all the time.
6: """
7: 
8: import numpy as np
9: 
10: 
11: def project_to_friction_cone(force, normal, mu):
12:     """Project a contact force onto the Coulomb friction cone.
13: 
14:     A fingertip can only push, and it can only carry tangential force up to
15:     ``mu`` times the normal force. Everything a contact-aware controller
16:     commands has to be clipped to that set first.
17: 
18:     Split the force at the contact into its normal and tangential parts,
19:     where ``n`` is ``normal`` after normalising::
20: 
21:         f_n = dot(force, n)
22:         f_t = force - f_n * n
23: 
24:     Three cases, and all three have to come out right:
25: 
32:            s   = (mu * norm(f_t) + f_n) / (mu**2 + 1)
33:            out = s * n + mu * s * f_t / norm(f_t)
34: 
35:     Case 3 is where the wrong answers live. Rescaling the whole vector until
36:     it fits also shrinks the normal component, which is not a projection and
37:     quietly weakens the grasp.
38: 
39:     ``force`` and ``normal`` are ``(3,)``; ``normal`` need not be unit
40:     length. ``mu >= 0``.
41: 
42:     Returns a ``(3,)`` array.
43:     """
44:     raise NotImplementedError("TODO: write this function")

11: def project_to_friction_cone(force, normal, mu):
12:     """Project a contact force onto the Coulomb friction cone.
13: 
14:     A fingertip can only push, and it can only carry tangential force up to
15:     ``mu`` times the normal force. Everything a contact-aware controller
16:     commands has to be clipped to that set first.
17: 
18:     Split the force at the contact into its normal and tangential parts,
19:     where ``n`` is ``normal`` after normalising::
20: 
21:         f_n = dot(force, n)
22:         f_t = force - f_n * n
23: 
24:     Three cases, and all three have to come out right:
25: 
32:            s   = (mu * norm(f_t) + f_n) / (mu**2 + 1)
33:            out = s * n + mu * s * f_t / norm(f_t)
34: 
35:     Case 3 is where the wrong answers live. Rescaling the whole vector until
36:     it fits also shrinks the normal component, which is not a projection and
37:     quietly weakens the grasp.
38: 
39:     ``force`` and ``normal`` are ``(3,)``; ``normal`` need not be unit
40:     length. ``mu >= 0``.
41: 
42:     Returns a ``(3,)`` array.
43:     """
44:     # >>> solution
45:     f = np.asarray(force, dtype=np.float64)
46:     n = np.asarray(normal, dtype=np.float64)
47:     n = n / np.linalg.norm(n)
48:     f_n = float(f @ n)

15: /**
16:  * Inspired by gazebo::physics::Gripper, this plugin fixes an object which is grasped to the
17:  * robot hand to avoid problems with physics engines and to help the object staying in
18:  * the robot hand without slipping out.
19:  *
20:  * This is a *model* plugin, so you have to load the model plugin from the robot URDF:
21:  *
22:  * ```xml
23:  *   <gazebo>
24:  *       <plugin name="gazebo_grasp_fix" filename="libgazebo_grasp_fix.so">
25:  *          <arm>
26:  *              <arm_name>name-of-arm</arm_name>
27:  *              <palm_link> hand_link_name  </palm_link>
28:  *              <gripper_link> finger_index_link_1 </gripper_link>
29:  *              <gripper_link> finger_index_link_2 </gripper_link>
30:  *              <gripper_link> ... </gripper_link>
31:  *           </arm>
32:  *           <forces_angle_tolerance>100</forces_angle_tolerance>
33:  *           <update_rate>4</update_rate>
34:  *           <grip_count_threshold>4</grip_count_threshold>
35:  *           <max_grip_count>8</max_grip_count>
36:  *           <release_tolerance>0.005</release_tolerance>
37:  *           <disable_collisions_on_attach>false</disable_collisions_on_attach>
38:  *           <contact_topic>__default_topic__</contact_topic>
39:  *       </plugin>
40:  *   </gazebo>
41:  * ```
42:  *
43:  *    Description of the arguments:
44:  *
45:  *    - ``<arm>`` contains a collections of specification for each arm which can grasp one object (there may be several ``<arm>`` tags):
46:  *        - ``<arm_name>`` is the name of this arm. Has to be unique.
47:  *        - ``<palm_link>`` has to be the link to which the finger joints are attached.
48:  *        - ``<gripper_link>`` tags have to include -all- link names of the gripper/hand which are used to
49:  *              actively grasp objects (these are the links which determine whether a "grasp" exists according to
50:  *              above described criterion).
51:  *    - ``<update_rate>`` is the rate at which all contact points are checked against the "gripping criterion".
52:  *          Note that in-between such updates, existing contact points may be collected at
53:  *          a higher rate (the Gazebo world update rate). The ``update_rate`` is only the rate at
54:  *          which they are processed, which takes a bit of computation time, and therefore
55:  *          should be lower than the gazebo world update rate.
56:  *    - ``<forces_angle_tolerance>`` is the tolerance angle (in degrees) between two force vectors to be considered
57:  *           "opposing forces". If the angle is smaller than this, they are not opposing.
58:  *    - ``<grip_count_threshold>`` is number of times in the update loop (running at update_rate) that an object has
59:  *            to be detected as "gripped" in order to attach the object.
60:  *            Adjust this with the update rate.
62:  *            At each update iteration (running at update_rate), if the "gripping criterion" is
63:  *            met for an object, a counter for this object is increased. ``max_grip_count`` is
64:  *            the maximum number recorded for an object. As soon as the counter goes beyond this
65:  *            number, the counter is stopped. As soon as the "gripping criterion" does not
66:  *            hold any more, the number will start to decrease again, (by 1 each time the object
67:  *            is detected as "not grasped" in an update iteration). So this counter is
68:  *            like a "buffer" which, when it is full, maintains the state, and when it is empty,
69:  *            again, the object is released.
70:  *            This should be at least double of ``grip_count_threshold``.
71:  *    - ``<release_tolerance>`` is the distance which the gripper links are allowed to move away from the object
72:  *            during- a grasp without the object being detached, even if there are currently no
73:  *            actual contacts on the object. This condition can happen if the fingers "wobble"
74:  *            or move ever so slightly away from the object, and therefore the "gripping criterion"
75:  *            fails in a few subsequent update iterations. This setting is to make the behaviour more
76:  *            stable.
77:  *            Setting this number too high will also lead to the object not being detached even
78:  *            if the grippers have opened up to release it, so use this with care.
79:  *    - ``<disable_collisions_on_attach>`` can be used for the following:
80:  *            When an object is attached, collisions with it may be disabled, in case the
81:  *            robot still keeps wobbling.
82:  *    - ``<contact_topic>`` is the gazebo topic of contacts. Should normally be left at -\_\_default_topic\_\_-.
83:  *
84:  * Current limitations:
87:  *  - Only partial support for an object cannot be gripped with two grippers (release condition may be
88:  *     triggered wrongly, or not at all, if two grippers are involved)

90:  * \author Jennifer Buehler
91:  */

107:         # largest minimum resisted wrench based on the GWS constructed incrementally from the minkowski sum of the contact wrenches and the total time taken
108:         # in the case of non force closure grasp, the quality is returned as 0.0
109:         if method == "Inc_minkowski":
110:             grasp_quality_4, time_4 = igws.calculate_minkowski_incremental_gws()
111:             quality_dict["Inc_minkowski"] = grasp_quality_4
112: 
113:         
114:     
115:     return quality_dict
116: '''
117:     P.S:
118: 
119:     With just three initial primitive wrenches and GWS constructed incrementally from the Minkowski sum of the wrenches,
120:     a quality approximately equivalent to that of the one computed from a pure Minkowski GWS with eight primitive wrenches
121:     can be achieved in almost half the time.

11:     """
12:     Hierarchical skeleton description.
13:     Stores joint names, parent indices, and a reference pose (local transforms).
14:     """
15:     def __init__(self, num_joints, joint_names, parent_indices, local_transforms : np.ndarray | list):
16:         """
17:         Initialize a Skeleton object with joint hierarchy and transformation data.
18:         Args:
19:             num_joints (int): The total number of joints in the skeleton.
20:             joint_names (list): A list of names for each joint. Must have length equal to num_joints.
21:             parent_indices (array-like): An array of parent joint indices for each joint, stored as int32.
22:                 Must have length equal to num_joints.
23:             local_transforms (np.ndarray | list): Local transformation matrices for the skeleton joints.
24:                 Can be a numpy array or list. Must have length equal to num_joints along the first axis.
25:                 Will be converted to float32 numpy array.
26:         Raises:
27:             ValueError: If the length of joint_names does not match num_joints.
28:             ValueError: If the length of parent_indices does not match num_joints.
29:             ValueError: If the length of local_transforms does not match num_joints.
30:         """
31:         self._num_joints = int(num_joints)
32:         self.joint_names = list(joint_names)
33:         self.parent_indices = np.asarray(parent_indices, dtype=np.int32)
34: 
35:         self.up_axis = wp.vec3(0, 0, 1)
36:         self.forward_axis = wp.vec3(0, -1, 0)
37: 
38:         if len(self.joint_names) != self._num_joints:
39:             raise ValueError(

42:             )
43: 
44:         if len(self.parent_indices) != self._num_joints:
45:             raise ValueError(

47:                 f"is not equal to num_joints [{self._num_joints}]"
48:             )

50:         if isinstance(local_transforms, np.ndarray):
51:             if local_transforms.shape[0] != self._num_joints:
52:                 raise ValueError(

54:                     f"is not equal to num_joints [{self._num_joints}]"

47: @wp.func
48: def compute_bone_lines(
49:     in_pyramid_vertices : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec3),
50:     in_offset           : wp.int32,
51:     in_joint_t          : wp.vec3,
52:     in_parent_t         : wp.vec3,
53:     out_line_starts     : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec3),
54:     out_line_ends       : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec3)
55: ):
56:     diff = wp.sub(in_parent_t, in_joint_t)
57:     q = wp.quat_between_vectors(wp.vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), wp.normalize(diff))
58: 
59:     length = wp.length(diff)
60:     width = length / 20.0
61: 
62:     compute_pyramid_vertices(
63:         in_pyramid_vertices, wp.transform(in_joint_t, q), wp.vec3(width, width, length * 0.8),
64:         in_offset, out_line_starts, out_line_ends)
65: 
66:     compute_pyramid_vertices(
67:         in_pyramid_vertices, wp.transform(in_parent_t, q), wp.vec3(width, width, -length * 0.2),
68:         in_offset + 8, out_line_starts, out_line_ends)
69: 
70: 
71: @wp.kernel
72: def _update_skeleton_lines_kernel(
73:     in_pyramid_vertices  : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec3),
74:     in_global_transforms : wp.array(dtype=wp.transform),
75:     in_bone_indices      : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec2i),
76:     out_line_starts      : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec3),
77:     out_line_ends        : wp.array(dtype=wp.vec3)
78: ):
79:     tid = wp.tid()
80:     bone = in_bone_indices[tid]
81: 
82:     compute_bone_lines(
83:          in_pyramid_vertices,
84:          tid * _const_pyramid_vertex_count,
85:          in_global_transforms[bone.y].p,
86:          in_global_transforms[bone.x].p,
87:          out_line_starts,
88:          out_line_ends)
89:

91: class SkeletonRenderer(BaseRenderer):
92:     """Renders a skeleton as pyramid-shaped bone lines."""
93: 
94:     def __init__(self, skeleton: Skeleton, masked_indices=None):
95:         super().__init__()
96:         self.skeleton = skeleton
97:         self.bones = self._build_bones(masked_indices)
98:         count = len(self.bones) * _const_pyramid_vertex_count
99:         self.line_starts = wp.zeros(count, dtype=wp.vec3)
100:         self.line_ends = wp.zeros(count, dtype=wp.vec3)
101:         self.parent_indices = wp.array(self.skeleton.parent_indices, dtype=wp.int32)
102: 
103:     def draw(self, viewer, skeleton_instance: SkeletonInstance, id: wp.int32):
104:         """Compute and display bone lines for the given skeleton pose."""
105:         if skeleton_instance.skeleton != self.skeleton:
106:             raise ValueError(f"[ERROR]: SkeletonInstance.skeleton [{skeleton_instance.skeleton}] is not equal to SkeletonRenderer.skeleton [{self.skeleton}]")
107: 
108:         global_transforms = skeleton_instance.compute_global_transforms()
109:         wp.launch(
110:             _update_skeleton_lines_kernel,
111:             dim=len(self.bones),
112:             inputs=[
113:                 _const_pyramid_vertices,
114:                 wp.array(global_transforms, dtype=wp.transform),
115:                 self.bones],
116:             outputs=[self.line_starts, self.line_ends])
117: 
118:         name = f"/skeleton_{id}"
119:         self._register_unique_id(name)
120:         viewer.log_lines(name, self.line_starts, self.line_ends, skeleton_instance.color)
121: 
122:     def clear(self, viewer):
123:         """Remove all skeleton lines from the viewer."""
124:         self._clear(viewer.lines)
125: 
126:     def _build_bones(self, mask_indices):
127:         mask = set(mask_indices) if mask_indices is not None else set()
128:         bones=[]
129:         for idx in range(1, self.skeleton.num_joints):
130:             parent_idx = self.skeleton.joint_parent(idx)
131:             if (idx in mask or parent_idx in mask):
132:                 continue
133:             bones.append(wp.vec2i(parent_idx, idx))
134: 
135:         return wp.array(bones, dtype=wp.vec2i)

309: class DexPilotOptimizer(Optimizer):
310:     """Retargeting optimizer using the method proposed in DexPilot
311: 
312:     This is a broader adaptation of the original optimizer delineated in the DexPilot paper.
313:     While the initial DexPilot study focused solely on the four-fingered Allegro Hand, this version of the optimizer
314:     embraces the same principles for both four-fingered and five-fingered hands. It projects the distance between the
315:     thumb and the other fingers to facilitate more stable grasping.
316:     Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.03135
317: 
318:     Args:
319:         robot:
320:         target_joint_names:
321:         finger_tip_link_names:
322:         wrist_link_name:
323:         gamma:
324:         project_dist:
325:         escape_dist:
326:         eta1:
327:         eta2:
328:         scaling:
329:     """
330: 
331:     retargeting_type = "DEXPILOT"
332: 
333:     def __init__(
334:         self,
335:         robot: RobotWrapper,
336:         target_joint_names: List[str],
337:         finger_tip_link_names: List[str],
338:         wrist_link_name: str,
339:         target_link_human_indices: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
340:         huber_delta=0.03,
341:         norm_delta=4e-3,
342:         # DexPilot parameters
343:         # gamma=2.5e-3,
344:         project_dist=0.03,
345:         escape_dist=0.05,
346:         eta1=1e-4,
347:         eta2=3e-2,
348:         scaling=1.0,
349:     ):
350:         if len(finger_tip_link_names) < 2 or len(finger_tip_link_names) > 5:
351:             raise ValueError(
352:                 f"DexPilot optimizer can only be applied to hands with 2 to 5 fingers, but got "
353:                 f"{len(finger_tip_link_names)} fingers."
354:             )
355:         self.num_fingers = len(finger_tip_link_names)
356: 
357:         origin_link_index, task_link_index = self.generate_link_indices(
358:             self.num_fingers
359:         )
360: 
361:         if target_link_human_indices is None:

372:         self.scaling = scaling

409:         """
410:         Example:
411:         >>> generate_link_indices(4)
412:         ([2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 4])

21: /// @file linear_skinning.h
22: /// Functions for linear blend skinning (Skeletal Subspace Deformation)
23: ///
24: /// Linear blend skinning (LBS), also known as Skeletal Subspace Deformation (SSD),
25: /// is a technique used in character animation to deform a mesh based on an underlying
26: /// skeleton. Each vertex in the mesh is influenced by one or more joints, with weights
27: /// determining how much influence each joint has on the vertex's final position.
28: ///

28: def compute_contact_metrics(skeleton_data: np.ndarray, fps: int = 30):
29:     """
30:     Compute three core contact-related metrics for bimanual hand motion.
31: 
32:     Analyzes the skeleton sequence to detect contact events between hands
33:     and computes statistics about contact patterns.
34: 
35:     Args:
44:     T = skeleton_data.shape[0]
45:     hand_left = skeleton_data[:, 0, :, :]   # (T, 21, 3)
46:     hand_right = skeleton_data[:, 1, :, :]  # (T, 21, 3)
47: 
48:     # ========== Pre-compute distances ==========
49:     # 1. Distance between fingertips
50:     fingertip_distances = np.zeros(T)
51:     for t in range(T):
52:         left_tips = hand_left[t, FINGER_TIP_INDICES, :]
53:         right_tips = hand_right[t, FINGER_TIP_INDICES, :]
54:         dist_matrix = cdist(left_tips, right_tips)
55:         fingertip_distances[t] = np.min(dist_matrix)
56: 
57:     # 2. Finger-palm distance
58:     finger_palm_distances = np.zeros(T)
59:     for t in range(T):
60:         # Left fingertips to right palm
61:         min_dists_lr = []
62:         for tip_idx in FINGER_TIP_INDICES:
63:             tip_pos = hand_left[t, tip_idx, :]
64:             palm_points = hand_right[t, PALM_INDICES, :]
65:             dists = np.linalg.norm(palm_points - tip_pos, axis=1)
66:             min_dists_lr.append(np.min(dists))
67: 
68:         # Right fingertips to left palm
69:         min_dists_rl = []
70:         for tip_idx in FINGER_TIP_INDICES:
71:             tip_pos = hand_right[t, tip_idx, :]
72:             palm_points = hand_left[t, PALM_INDICES, :]
73:             dists = np.linalg.norm(palm_points - tip_pos, axis=1)
74:             min_dists_rl.append(np.min(dists))
75: 
76:         finger_palm_distances[t] = min(min(min_dists_lr), min(min_dists_rl))
77: 
78:     # ========== Metric 1: Contact Ratio ==========
79:     finger_finger_contact = fingertip_distances < FINGER_FINGER_CONTACT
80:     finger_palm_contact = finger_palm_distances < FINGER_PALM_CONTACT
81: 
82:     interaction_mask = finger_finger_contact | finger_palm_contact
83:     contact_ratio = np.sum(interaction_mask) / T
84: 
85:     # ========== Metric 3: Avg Contact Duration (seconds) ==========
86:     # Find continuous contact segments
87:     segments = []
88:     in_contact = False
89:     start = 0
90: 
91:     for t in range(T):
92:         if interaction_mask[t] and not in_contact:
93:             start = t

2: hand_retarget.py
3: ================
4: Whole-hand retargeting on top of `thumb_retarget`.
5: 
6: Structural note
7: ---------------
8: A finger here is AA + parallel-3R. That is the SAME structure as the thumb's
9: yaw + parallel-3R: one joint whose axis is perpendicular to the three parallel
10: flexion axes, placed proximal to them. So `ThumbKinematics` / `ThumbIK` apply
11: verbatim -- only link lengths, joint limits and `R_off` differ. Define each
12: digit's base frame so that
13: 
14:     +z  = the AA (spread) axis
15:     -y  = the three parallel flexion axes
16:     +x  = the neutral pointing direction
17: 
18: and the closed-form solver needs no changes. `Finger1P3R` below is just an
19: alias; the code does not care whether you call the first joint yaw or pitch.
20: 
21: Retargeting policy
22: ------------------
23: Thumb:   tracked absolutely, as accurately as the hardware allows.
24: Fingers: a blend of
25:            (a) absolute scaled position, and
26:            (b) a position defined relative to the THUMB'S ACHIEVED fingertip,
27: with the blend weight rising as the human's thumb-finger distance shrinks.
28: 
29: Two things this gets right that a naive version does not:
30: 
31: 1. The relative anchor is the thumb's ACHIEVED pose (FK after clamping and
32:    rate limiting), never its commanded target. When the thumb saturates -- which
33:    is exactly when a pinch is being attempted -- anchoring on the command would
34:    place the finger relative to a pose the thumb never reached, and the pinch
35:    fails precisely when it matters most.
36: 
37: 2. Human pinch distance is not zero. Nail- or pad-frame separation at a firm
38:    human pinch is typically 15-25 mm, and the robot's own pads have thickness
39:    too. `PinchMap` maps human separation onto robot separation with both
40:    contact offsets accounted for, so "human contact" maps to "robot contact"
41:    rather than to interpenetration or to a permanent gap.
42: """

222: def convert_grasp_frame(frame2matrix, matrix2grasp):
223:     """Function for converting from one grasp frame to another.
224: 
225:     This is useful as transforming grasp positions requires multiplication of
226:     4x4 matrix, while contact normals (orientation) are multiplication of 3x3
227:     components (i.e. without positional components).
228:     """
229: 
230:     if matrix2grasp.ndim == 1:

232: 
233:     # A grasp is contacts, normals, and forces (3), and has (x,y,z) components
234:     n_fingers = int(matrix2grasp.shape[1] / 6)
235:     contact_points = matrix2grasp[0, :n_fingers * 3].reshape(3, 3)
236:     contact_normals = matrix2grasp[0, n_fingers * 3:n_fingers * 6].reshape(3, 3)
237: 
238:     # Append a 1 to end of contacts for easier multiplication
239:     contact_points = np.hstack([contact_points, np.ones((3, 1))])
240: 
241:     # Convert positions, normals, and forces to object reference frame
242:     points = np.zeros((n_fingers, 3))
243:     normals = np.zeros(points.shape)
244: 
245:     for i in range(n_fingers):
246: 
247:         points[i] = np.dot(frame2matrix, contact_points[i:i + 1].T)[:3].T
248:         normals[i] = np.dot(frame2matrix[:3, :3], contact_normals[i:i + 1].T).T
249: 
250:     return np.vstack([points, normals]).reshape(1, -1)

1: """Build a synthetic, license-free example HOI bundle (examples/sample.npz).
2: 
3: A zero-shape MANO right hand descends onto a small box and curls its fingers,
4: while the box sits on the table. Purely procedural — no dataset assets — just to
5: show the bundle format and let `replicate.py --bundle` run out of the box.
6: 
7: Bundle keys:
8:   betas(10,), hand_pose(T,48 axis-angle), trans(T,3), side,
9:   object_verts(V,3)+object_faces(F,3), object_poses(T,7 [x,y,z,qw,qx,qy,qz]),
10:   object_color(3,)
11: """
12: import numpy as np
13: from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation as R
14: 
21: v[:, 2] += hz                                   # bottom on the table
22: F = np.array([[0, 1, 3], [0, 3, 2], [4, 6, 7], [4, 7, 5], [0, 4, 5], [0, 5, 1],
23:               [2, 3, 7], [2, 7, 6], [1, 5, 7], [1, 7, 3], [0, 2, 6], [0, 6, 4]])
24: object_poses = np.tile([0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0], (T, 1)).astype(np.float32)  # static
25: 
26: # --- hand: descend onto the box, palm down, fingers curl 0 -> ~1 rad ---
27: # MANO rest right hand: fingers point -X, palm faces -Y. R_x(+90deg) turns the
28: # palm to -Z (down) while fingers keep pointing -X, so the hand descends onto the
29: # box from above with fingers reaching across its top.
30: betas = np.zeros(10, np.float32)
31: global_orient = np.tile(R.from_euler("X", np.pi/2).as_rotvec(), (T, 1))
32: s = np.linspace(0, 1, T)[:, None]
33: # wrist = trans + rest_j_wrist(~[0.096,0,0]); box spans x[-0.04,0.04] at origin, so
34: # put the wrist just +X of the box and descend onto it.
35: trans = (1 - s) * np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.22]) + s * np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.085])
36: 
37: curl = np.linspace(0.0, 1.1, T)                  # flexion ramp (rot about local z)
38: finger = np.zeros((T, 15, 3), np.float32)
39: finger[:, :, 2] = curl[:, None]                  # curl every finger joint
40: hand_pose = np.concatenate([global_orient, finger.reshape(T, 45)], axis=1).astype(np.float32)
41: 
42: bundle = dict(betas=betas, hand_pose=hand_pose, trans=trans.astype(np.float32),
43:               side="right", object_verts=v, object_faces=F,
44:               object_poses=object_poses,
45:               object_color=np.array([0.2, 0.5, 0.85], np.float32))
46: np.savez("examples/sample.npz", **bundle)
47: 
48: # also a human-readable JSON copy (viewable on GitHub without downloading)
49: import json
50: json.dump({k: (v.tolist() if isinstance(v, np.ndarray) else v)
51:            for k, v in bundle.items()}, open("examples/sample.json", "w"), indent=1)

3: 覆盖：inspire / allegro / shadow / svh / leap / ability / panda
4: 
5: 每个机型生成三种动作序列（全部保存为 .rrd）：
6:   grasp  —— 五指同步抓握（张开 → 握紧 → 张开）
7:   wave   —— 手指依次弯曲（波浪效果）
8:   pinch  —— 拇指与各指依次对捏
9: 
10: 运行方式（在项目根目录执行）：
11:   # 一键生成所有机型所有动作
12:   python examples/demo_retarget_hands.py --all
13: 
14:   # 单机型单动作（实时查看）
15:   python examples/demo_retarget_hands.py --hand shadow_hand --mode wave
16: 
17:   # 单机型保存 rrd
18:   python examples/demo_retarget_hands.py --hand ability_hand --mode grasp --save
19: 
20: 生成的 .rrd 文件保存在 output/demo/ 目录，用以下命令打开：
21:   rerun output/demo/<hand>_<mode>.rrd
22: """

24: import argparse

28: import numpy as np
29: 
39: def smooth_pulse(t_norm: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
40:     """0→1→0 平滑脉冲（sin²），t_norm ∈ [0,1]"""
41:     return np.sin(np.pi * t_norm) ** 2
42: 
43: 
44: def make_grasp_seq(dof, fps, duration, flex_map, abduct_map=None):
45:     """
46:     抓握序列：所有弯曲关节同步 0→max→0。
47:     flex_map:   {dof_index: amplitude}
48:     abduct_map: {dof_index: amplitude}（可选，外展/内收）
49:     """
50:     T = int(fps * duration)
51:     t = np.linspace(0, 1, T)
52:     pulse = smooth_pulse(t)
53:     seq = np.zeros((T, dof))
54:     for idx, amp in flex_map.items():
55:         seq[:, idx] = pulse * amp
57:         for idx, amp in abduct_map.items():
58:             seq[:, idx] = pulse * amp
59:     return seq
60: 
61: 
62: def make_wave_seq(dof, fps, duration, finger_groups):
63:     """
64:     波浪序列：每根手指依次错开相位弯曲。
65:     finger_groups: list of (dof_indices, amplitude, phase_offset)
66:     """
67:     T = int(fps * duration)
68:     t = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, T)
69:     seq = np.zeros((T, dof))
70:     for dof_indices, amp, phase in finger_groups:
71:         wave = amp * np.clip(np.sin(t - phase), 0, 1)
72:         for idx in dof_indices:
73:             seq[:, idx] = wave
74:     return seq
75: 
76: 
77: def make_pinch_seq(dof, fps, duration, thumb_map, finger_groups):
78:     """
79:     对捏序列：拇指保持弯曲，各指依次与拇指对捏。
80:     thumb_map:     {dof_index: amplitude}  拇指全程保持
81:     finger_groups: list of (dof_indices, amplitude, phase_offset)  各指依次弯曲
82:     """
83:     T = int(fps * duration)
84:     t = np.linspace(0, 1, T)
85:     pulse = smooth_pulse(t)
86:     seq = np.zeros((T, dof))
87:     # 拇指全程保持弯曲
88:     for idx, amp in thumb_map.items():
89:         seq[:, idx] = pulse * amp
90:     # 各指依次对捏（用 sin² 脉冲，错开相位）
91:     n = len(finger_groups)
92:     for i, (dof_indices, amp) in enumerate(finger_groups):
93:         # 每根手指占 1/n 时间窗口，用高斯脉冲
94:         center = (i + 0.5) / n
95:         width = 0.15
96:         pinch = np.exp(-((t - center) ** 2) / (2 * width ** 2))
97:         pinch = pinch / pinch.max()
98:         for idx in dof_indices:
99:             seq[:, idx] = pinch * amp
100:     return seq
101:

1: """Reproducible, hardware-free Gate 1--3 Panda + Allegro grasp validation.
2: 
3: The live teleoperation path remains deliberately untouched.  This module owns
4: only scripted simulator experiments and never constructs a SpaceMouse or a
5: camera worker.  A single runner executes the gates in order:
6:

8: ``Gate 2`` evaluates a temporarily supported static hand grasp after the
9: support is removed; and ``Gate 3`` performs the same grasp through a scripted
10: world-frame OSC trajectory.

65: def estimate_finger_curl(landmarks: Sequence[Any], ids: Sequence[int]) -> float:
66:     """Legacy angle-plus-distance curl estimator; 0=open and 1=closed."""
67:     mcp, pip, _dip, tip = (_point(landmarks[index]) for index in ids)
68:     angle_curl = float(np.clip((165.0 - _angle_degrees(mcp - pip, tip - pip)) / 95.0, 0.0, 1.0))
69:     wrist = _point(landmarks[0])
70:     distance_ratio = float(np.linalg.norm(tip - wrist) / (np.linalg.norm(mcp - wrist) + 1e-6))
71:     distance_curl = 1.0 - float(np.clip((distance_ratio - 1.1) / 1.1, 0.0, 1.0))
72:     return float(np.clip(0.75 * angle_curl + 0.25 * distance_curl, 0.0, 1.0))

75: def estimate_all_finger_curls(landmarks: Sequence[Any]) -> np.ndarray:
76:     if len(landmarks) != 21:
77:         raise ValueError("MediaPipe hand input must contain exactly 21 landmarks")
78:     index = estimate_finger_curl(landmarks, (5, 6, 7, 8))
79:     middle = estimate_finger_curl(landmarks, (9, 10, 11, 12))
80:     ring = estimate_finger_curl(landmarks, (13, 14, 15, 16))
81:     pinky = estimate_finger_curl(landmarks, (17, 18, 19, 20))

86: def curls_to_allegro_targets(curls: Sequence[float], lower_limits: Sequence[float], upper_limits: Sequence[float]) -> np.ndarray:
87:     """Apply the exact legacy 4-curl / 16-target weighting with model limits."""
88:     curls = np.asarray(curls, dtype=np.float64)
89:     lower = np.asarray(lower_limits, dtype=np.float64)
90:     upper = np.asarray(upper_limits, dtype=np.float64)
91:     if curls.shape != (4,) or lower.shape != (16,) or upper.shape != (16,):
92:         raise ValueError("expected curls (4,) and lower/upper limits (16,)")
93:     if not np.all(np.isfinite(curls)) or not np.all(np.isfinite(lower)) or not np.all(np.isfinite(upper)) or not np.all(upper > lower):
94:         raise ValueError("curls and joint limits must be finite, ordered values")
95:     curls = np.clip(curls, 0.0, 1.0)
96:     opened = np.clip(np.zeros(16), lower, upper)
97:     targets = opened.copy()
98:     for finger in range(3):
99:         segment = slice(finger * 4, finger * 4 + 4)
100:         targets[segment] = opened[segment] + curls[finger] * NORMAL_FINGER_WEIGHTS * (upper[segment] - opened[segment])
101:     targets[12:16] = opened[12:16] + curls[3] * THUMB_WEIGHTS * (upper[12:16] - opened[12:16])
102:     return np.clip(targets, lower, upper)

35: # Synthetic MANO-topology grasp around a primitive.                            #

37: def make_synthetic_grasp(kind="cylinder", n_obj=50, seed=0, hand_scale=0.16):
38:     """Build a plausible power/precision grasp whose fingertips contact the object.
39: 
40:     The hand is intentionally a *different size* from the Wuji hand to exercise the
41:     embodiment gap.  All 21 keypoints are returned in MANO order.
42:     """
43:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
44:     if kind == "cylinder":
45:         # tall-ish can: height prevents fingers from cheating over the top rim,
46:         # so the retargeted grasp must press the lateral wall like the human.
47:         obj = Cylinder(center=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], radius=0.042, hz=0.11)
48:         R = obj.radius
49:     elif kind == "sphere":
50:         obj = Sphere(center=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], radius=0.05)
51:         R = obj.radius
52:     else:
53:         raise ValueError(kind)
54: 
55:     # Wrist sits on the -x side, fingers wrap toward +/-x around the object.
56:     wrist = np.array([-(R + 0.085), 0.0, -0.01], np.float32)
57: 
58:     # The four fingers (index..pinky): contact angles around the cylinder near the
59:     # front (angle pi = -x side), spread in height(z) and wrap angle.
60:     # name : (wrap_angle_rad, height_z, y_knuckle).  Thumb opposes from +y side.
61:     finger_specs = {
62:         "thumb":  (np.pi * 0.5,  0.015,  0.045),
63:         "index":  (np.pi - 0.55, 0.045,  0.028),
64:         "middle": (np.pi - 0.20, 0.050,  0.010),
65:         "ring":   (np.pi + 0.15, 0.040, -0.010),
66:         "pinky":  (np.pi + 0.50, 0.028, -0.030),
67:     }
68:     kpts = np.zeros((21, 3), np.float32)
69:     kpts[0] = wrist
70: 
71:     def surface_point(ang, z):
72:         if kind == "cylinder":
73:             return obj.center + np.array([R * np.cos(ang), R * np.sin(ang), z], np.float32)
74:         d = np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang) * 0.6, z / max(R, 1e-6)])
75:         d = d / np.linalg.norm(d)
76:         return (obj.center + R * d).astype(np.float32)
77: 
78:     def place_finger(slot, mcp, tip, bulge):
79:         outward = mcp - obj.center
80:         outward = outward / (np.linalg.norm(outward) + 1e-8)
81:         pip = 0.45 * mcp + 0.55 * tip + bulge * outward
82:         dip = 0.18 * mcp + 0.82 * tip + 0.5 * bulge * outward
83:         base = 1 + slot * 4
84:         kpts[base:base + 4] = np.stack([mcp, pip, dip, tip])
85: 
86:     for name, (ang, z, yk) in finger_specs.items():
87:         slot = MANO_GROUPS.index(name)
88:         tip = surface_point(ang, z)
89:         mcp = wrist + np.array([0.035, yk, z * 0.5], np.float32)
90:         place_finger(slot, mcp.astype(np.float32), tip, bulge=0.011)
91:

4: -> 21 robot keypoints in MANO order, plus all link transforms for rendering.
5: 
6: MANO 21-keypoint order (MediaPipe convention) used throughout:
7:     0  wrist
8:     1-4    thumb  (MCP, PIP, DIP, TIP)
9:     5-8    index
10:     9-12   middle
11:     13-16  ring
12:     17-20  pinky
13: """

16: import torch

21: # Which robot link frame represents each MANO keypoint.  finger1 = thumb.
22: # We use link2/link3/link4/tip as the four per-finger joints (link1 is a short
23: # coupling near the palm).
24: _FINGER_OF_MANO = {  # mano finger -> wuji finger index
25:     "thumb": 1, "index": 2, "middle": 3, "ring": 4, "pinky": 5,
26: }
27: _MANO_GROUPS = ["thumb", "index", "middle", "ring", "pinky"]
28: 
29: 
30: def _keypoint_frames():
31:     frames = ["right_palm_link"]  # 0: wrist
32:     for g in _MANO_GROUPS:
33:         f = _FINGER_OF_MANO[g]
34:         frames += [f"right_finger{f}_link2",   # MCP
35:                    f"right_finger{f}_link3",   # PIP
36:                    f"right_finger{f}_link4",   # DIP
37:                    f"right_finger{f}_tip_link"]  # TIP
38:     return frames  # length 21
39: 
40: 
41: # Bones along each finger: (wrist|MCP|PIP|DIP)->next, as index pairs into the 21.
42: def _bones():
43:     bones = []
44:     for fi in range(5):
45:         base = 1 + fi * 4
46:         chain = [0, base, base + 1, base + 2, base + 3]  # wrist + 4 joints
47:         for a, b in zip(chain[:-1], chain[1:]):
48:             bones.append((a, b))
49:     return bones  # 5 fingers x 4 = 20 bones
50: 
51: 
52: # Adjacent bone pairs along each finger (for the relative bone-direction loss).
53: def _adjacent_bone_pairs():
54:     pairs = []
55:     for fi in range(5):
56:         b0 = fi * 4  # first bone index of this finger in _bones()
57:         for k in range(3):  # (b0,b1),(b1,b2),(b2,b3)
58:             pairs.append((b0 + k, b0 + k + 1))
59:     return pairs

64:         self.device, self.dtype = device, dtype

69:         self.n_joints = len(self.joint_names)              # 20
70:         self.kp_frames = _keypoint_frames()                # 21 frame names
71:         self.bones = _bones()
